newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- falls back to Wed. levels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- falls back to Wed. levels.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices lost early gains and were trading back at Wednesday's levels at midday Thursday, trader said.
"We're pretty much back to unchanged," one trader said, adding that activity levels were quiet. "There's not a lot out for the bid."
Munis rose with other fixed income markets early Thursday, gaining about 1/8 to 1/4 after an unexpected rise in new jobless claims, to 347,000, for the week ended June 14.

But the markets declined again after the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia said its index of business activity in the manufacturing sector rose to 25.2 in June from 1.6 in May. Economists had expected the figure to be just 7.3.
Treasury prices slipped after the number, with the government long bond down 6/32 at 99, moving the yield up to 6.70 percent.

Goldman Sachs & Co tentatively priced Thursday's largest negotiated deal, a $356 million sale of refunding bonds by the Municipal Assistance Corp. for New York City. The bonds priced at a 4.95 percent top yield in 2008.

On the competitive side, 12 sales totaling $136 million are scheduled. A $23 million Warren County Justice Center Expansion Corp., Ky., deal at 1100 EDT was the largest. Prudential Securities won the bonds and reoffered the 2029 terms at a 5.474 percent yield.

September municipal futures also turned negative at midday, losing 4/32 to 118-6/32. September Treasury bond futures lost 5/32 to 112, widening the MOB spread to 198 ticks from 197 at the close on Wednesday.

In secondary trading, Orange County, Fla., MBIA School Board 5-3/8s Certificates of Participation of 2022 were bid at 5.54 percent, unchanged from Wednesday. The bonds were bid up one basis point in early trade.
Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were bid at 99-1/2, up 1/8 from Wednesday but down slightly from earlier quotes on Thursday.
